Two bugs the fixtures had been catching unread: the insets did not turn with the frame, and `mongolianVert` stacked its columns in reverse

subPhases.title: Fidelity harness
subPhases.result: the gate had been reporting PASS over 155 slides while gating 152, because a slide the baseline had never heard of counted as unchanged; it now refuses to score one it holds no digest for, and `--record` needs a written reason and the exact count it will move. Every differing cell is charged to the shape that painted it, which found a third bad shape on `a03-fills-02` that two passes over its heatmap had missed and put numbers on two of 2.7's recorded open questions. The clock a slide draws moves 31 cells at maxD 6, an order of magnitude under the rasteriser's own noise. The Linux baseline is recorded and CI runs the gate, which caught two breaks a Windows-only run never could: the workflow had ordered Build after Lint, so `check` had been red on every push to main, a committed README linked to a gitignored file, and three of 3.7 font tests asserted what this machine has rather than what the code does

subPhases.title: First npm release: `render-svg` and `cli render`
subPhases.result: the plan called this a release and it was really a measurement: `render-svg` was already a pure string function that ran in Node, but text needed a canvas and there is none, so `pptx-studio render` reads the font own tables instead. That is a second measurement engine, and no real font can say what the first one does - Arial `hhea.ascender` and its `OS/2.usWinAscent` are both 1854 - so T13 built seven fonts that disagree with themselves on purpose and asked Chromium. The face box is `usWin`, or `sTypo` where `fsSelection` bit 7 is set (14/14, against 10/14 for `hhea`, which is what everybody writes first); pair kerning is GPOS where the font has a `kern` feature and the legacy table otherwise (42/42, against 36/42 for preferring the legacy one, which is the cheaper parse and wrong on every font carrying both); a width is each advance truncated and each kern rounded at 1/65536 px (252/252, against 88/252 for exact floats). The advance is linear in size to within 1.04e-4 px, which is the finding the whole approach rests on: the browser does not hint it. The reader reproduces all 252 widths exactly and 19 of 19 mutants die. Running the release path found that changesets/action renamed its four inputs, so Release had been red on every push to main since 0.1, and that no package carried a LICENSE or a NOTICE, which Apache-2.0 4(a) and 4(d) require and ours is not decorative - it carries POI attribution for the 187 presets Finishing it found that nothing had ever installed the eleven packages - pkg:qa inspects a tarball shape and apps/studio resolves through the link farm - so examples/nextjs-studio installs them from the registry instead, and 194 of 194 XML parts re-emit byte-identical through real tarballs. Consuming the published API from outside showed renderDeck taking the verb options rather than the drawing ones, which is now RenderDeckOptions and a breaking 0.2.0. Two of 0042 five open questions close: the ideographic baseline is the BASE ideo coordinate of the DFLT script and not the descent, 30 of 30, so the shipped reading was wrong on any face carrying one, and Chromium reads DFLT alone, never the run script, with no fall-through when it is absent; and trunc against floor is foreclosed by hmtx.advanceWidth being a UFWORD rather than unmeasured, so the probe 0042 asked for cannot be built. T14 then ran on a Linux runner for the first time and went red on three defects in shipped code: the reader skipped type 9 Extension GPOS lookups, so eighteen Lato faces got no kerning at all and measured Latin about 8 percent wide, silently; renderDeck threw CLI_NO_FACE on a machine holding 53 usable faces, where the whole point of the font guard is to substitute and report; and the face box is 75.8 px out on the descent of three Japanese faces, which is still open. It also refuted 0042 own width finding: all 3420 browser widths on Linux are whole pixels, so the claim that the browser does not hint the advance was true of seven fonts carrying no hinting program and never generalised, and the gate premise had to be re-derived from per-glyph rounding rather than from exactness. The next run answered the face box it had left open, and the answer was that the question was malformed: there is no one table. DirectWrite reads usWin and FreeType reads hhea, bit 7 moving both onto sTypo, and neither reading fits both platforms - 12/12 against Windows and 76/79 against Linux for the first, 79/79 and 7/12 for the second, missing by 75.8 px and 100 px on a 1000 px em. So the shipped reader was not wrong, it was answering for one rasteriser while running on the other, and metricsOf now takes the backend its host resolves. The Extension fix held: 228 width failures fell to 6, all on Lato, and those turned out to be the tolerance rather than the reader - the browser rounds the advance and the kern adjustment separately, so a run carries one rounding per glyph and one per applied kern. A joint rounding is refuted rather than assumed, because it cannot cost the 0.648 px a glyph Lato Thin measures where every kern-free sample stays under 0.45, and only a 2000 unit em shows it at all, since it puts every value on a half pixel exactly where a 1000 em is exact and a 2048 one cancels. Then the fix could not be released, and that was the more important defect. Nothing had ever executed a published package: pkg:qa reads a tarball manifest without installing or running it, apps/studio resolves workspace:^ through the link farm, and the example job installed from the registry, so it could only ever report on a version already shipped. Worse, it sat in the run the release gate reads, so the broken publish made CI red, which refused the release that would have fixed it - a monitor wired into a gate socket, blocking its own repair. The gate is now on the candidate: pack every package, install the tarballs into a scratch consumer with the scope pointed at a dead registry, refuse any resolution that is not one of this run tarballs by sha512, and run the example against them. Packing alone would not have been enough - pnpm pack rewrites workspace:^ to ^0.1.0, which the registry satisfies, so an unbumped package would have been silently tested against what is already published. The registry check keeps its job as a scheduled canary that can block nothing, and the release gate names the jobs it requires rather than reading a whole workflow conclusion.
subPhases.note: twelve packages on npm, every latest attested, the canary owned by an issue it opens on a red run and closes on a green one, the example manifest written by pnpm version-packages and refused by the candidate gate when it disagrees with the tree, and the root README saying so (ADR 0051). The face box rounds half up to a whole pixel at the size the browser reads it, 28 of 28 on two probes built off the pixel, and the no-BASE ideographic baseline is that rounded descent, 36 of 36; the CLI markup names the face each run was measured in, drawn first; a Windows runner re-takes T13 on every commit and the release requires it; Turbo did not serve a stale dist, three trials, and every job that scores dist builds with --force (ADR 0052). Still open, and why not here: the twelve versions published without provenance - ten at 0.1.0, cli@0.1.0, render-dom@0.0.0 - read neither in tools/release/registry/attestations.ts until npm deprecate marks them, which is one OTP per package and so a person; a trusted publisher revoked between releases is found by the next release and by nothing sooner, because npm has no read-only form of the question, npm trust list is OTP-only, and the preflight can only ask by minting tokens it never uses (ADR 0048, 0049); the candidate gate installs with one package manager on one Node (ADR 0046); no shaping, so Arabic and Devanagari measure wide and T14 records the ratio rather than gating it; macOS is measured by neither rasteriser and takes the DirectWrite reading by assumption until real-faces-macos is dispatched, whose first run is expected red on advance-quantum and names the table CoreText reads; and a deck rendered on one platform and viewed on another has two answers to the face box, which the markup now says the first face of.
